Left panel: the front view, Open pages: two cream pages of small, dense, blurred type, no pictures, no headings legible. Right panel: the back view, Closed book: plain dark-green cloth front board with a thin blind-stamped border and no title. The two views stand apart with wide empty space between them, not touching or overlapping, identical material, colour and wear in both, on a plain neutral mid-grey studio backdrop with soft even light. Under each panel a small plain label: FRONT under the left view, BACK under the right view; no other text outside the object. No people, no hands, no animals, no body parts anywhere in the picture; the object is the only subject. Overall visual style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.
